inventions: Staging: Sen has four chairs set out, having counted contributors from the attachments to Kade's filing.
Sen says Eli's oversight notice 'comes to my desk' and that she cannot promise it comes only to hers. This follows up the Ch23 bell without naming any recipient.

Sen says she called Aaron 'subject' in reports for six years, and that his cross-category trace was filed as instrument error for two years. The six years is consistent with Mara's Ch23 finding of six years of restricted listings.
Sen says she was twenty-five at the time of Contact Zero, consistent with the bronze showing her at twenty-six.
Mara knows the Directorate's name from a routing stamp in the precursor cards. The source has only 'I read.'
Sen tells Kade to enter the 'is Aaron alive' refusal on his Ch20 withholding index with 'Amara Sen' as the withholding authority.

Elena's inspectable-limit exchange: disclosure must be in person and carry no signal; they review it at the kitchen table when Kade is home at the break; any change about Aaron is shared the same day.
Elena's lines about giving death news 'the other way round' and building seventeen years on a cardboard box, drawing on the canonical box of effects with no body.
Kade heads his audit with Halden's Ch23 question. Amadi assigns the audit in pairs and tells Kade the question belongs to the room.
A House custom of leaving soup out for late returns, as unnamed background texture supporting the home/machine realization.
state_change_proposals: Kade, Mara, Eli and Sera now know: Contact Zero is nonhuman; Resonance science derives from it; the academies and the ladder have a strategic measurement function; the Continuity Directorate's origin and Sen's former membership; the 11.4-second twelve-person coupling and Aaron's boundary alteration; Sen saw Aaron after the official accident.
Kade's withholding index gains one entry, Aaron's present status, with Sen herself as the withholding authority.

Elena knows Aaron was Standard Eight, that Zero came from the same program, and that Sen saw him alive after the certificate date. She knows more exists, that the limit is Kade's own decision, and the conditions under which he will tell her.

Group protocol: no full disclosure without returning to the group first; no promise of permanent silence; Eli will not copy Sen's files; Mara will separate Alaric's facts from inference before contacting him.
Kade has begun deliberately withholding from Taren out of caution; Taren is visibly aware of it.
Amadi's class has an open audit of the twelve-source calibration set, with Kade assigned the sealed-attribution problem.
deviations: In the source, Sen says 'I do not know whether the official event killed him' and Kade tells Elena 'She says she does not know.' This draft has Sen state that the accident did not kill him, because she saw him afterward, and explicitly refuse to say whether he is alive now. This avoids an outright lie that Ch29–31 would contradict and keeps the alive/unknown tension the ledger requires. The editor should confirm it is acceptable.
Elena's first line in the source ('I was scared') is replaced by an echo of her rewritten Ch23 line, 'small felt safe', to match the rewritten seam.
The Julian disclosure-risk entry on the paper protocol was cut for length. The source's chronologically impossible aside about a Julian line Kade 'had not heard yet' was dropped.
The source's 'Do you practice being infuriating? / Long career' exchange and the soup small talk about Sera's Response observation and Mara's paper were cut for length.
Taren's 'I saw you' is left ambiguous ('It might even have been true'), where the source has 'True enough.' No new clue is asserted.
